description: Golden corpus for false-start / sentence-stem removal. Every cleaner (rules, Ollama, Gemini) is scored against these exact cases by tests/harness.py.

cases.input: Can we meet up on tuesday at 5, or actually, can we meet up on friday at 3.
cases.expected: Can we meet up on Friday at 3.
cases.note: The exact example from PRD v2.0 section 3.

cases.input: I'll send you the report tomorrow, or actually I'll send you the report on Monday.
cases.expected: I'll send you the report on Monday.

cases.input: the deploy goes out at noon, wait no, the deploy goes out at six.
cases.expected: The deploy goes out at six.

cases.input: We should ship the beta this week, actually, let's hold it until the audit clears.
cases.expected: Let's hold it until the audit clears.

cases.input: Put the config in the root folder, sorry I mean, we should keep it in the etc directory.
cases.expected: We should keep it in the etc directory.

cases.input: Let's meet Tuesday at 5, actually Friday at 3.
cases.expected: Let's meet Friday at 3.

cases.input: Order 12 units, or actually 20.
cases.expected: Order 20 units.

cases.input: Assign the ticket to Priya, or actually Marcus.
cases.expected: Assign the ticket to Marcus.

cases.input: um so we need to, you know, rebuild the index uh before friday
cases.expected: So we need to rebuild the index before Friday.

cases.input: it took, like, three hours to finish
cases.expected: It took three hours to finish.

cases.input: I like the new onboarding flow.
cases.expected: I like the new onboarding flow.
cases.note: Soft filler must not eat the verb 'like'.

cases.input: I actually finished the migration last night.
cases.expected: I actually finished the migration last night.
cases.note: Mid-clause 'actually' is emphasis, not a retraction.

cases.input: Take the second right after the bridge.
cases.expected: Take the second right after the bridge.
cases.note: 'right' is only a filler in discourse position.

cases.input: The cache warms on boot and the workers pick up jobs after that.
cases.expected: The cache warms on boot and the workers pick up jobs after that.

cases.input: The API is stable. We ship on tuesday, or actually we ship on thursday.
cases.expected: The API is stable. We ship on Thursday.
cases.note: A retraction must not reach back past the previous sentence.

cases.input: Call him at 4, or actually call him at 5, wait no, call him at 6.
cases.expected: Call him at 6.

cases.input: Book the small conference room, scratch that, we need the auditorium for this one.
cases.expected: We need the auditorium for this one.

cases.input: the thing is broken in a weird way, let me rephrase that, the parser drops trailing commas.
cases.expected: The parser drops trailing commas.

cases.input: We can revisit this next quarter, actually.
cases.expected: We can revisit this next quarter.
cases.note: Nothing follows the pivot, so nothing may be deleted.

cases.input: The build passes locally, or actually in staging too.
cases.expected: The build passes locally, in staging too.
cases.note: Additive 'actually': no slot overlap, so we drop only the pivot rather than guess.

cases.input: run the PostgreSQL migration on the iOS build, um, before the gRPC cutover
cases.expected: Run the PostgreSQL migration on the iOS build, before the gRPC cutover.
cases.note: Capitalization of existing technical terms must never be altered.

cases.input: I I think the deploy goes out at noon.
cases.expected: I think the deploy goes out at noon.

cases.input: the the the build passes locally.
cases.expected: The build passes locally.

cases.input: can we can we meet on Friday at 3.
cases.expected: Can we meet on Friday at 3.

cases.input: can we can we meet on tuesday at 5, or actually, can we meet on friday at 3.
cases.expected: Can we meet on Friday at 3.
cases.note: Stutter collapse must run before pivot detection, or the doubled clause looks like a re-anchor.

cases.input: He had had enough of the flaky tests.
cases.expected: He had had enough of the flaky tests.
cases.note: Real English doubling; collapsing it changes the tense.

cases.input: That was very very slow.
cases.expected: That was very very slow.
cases.note: Repeating an intensifier is emphasis, not a disfluency.

cases.input: The cat sat on the mat.
cases.expected: The cat sat on the mat.
